title: Review Ops: Humans at Scale
objective: After this lesson you will be able to sample by risk (uncertainty + stakes + random baseline), design queues with SLAs, build reviewer UX that decides fast and logs richly, and close the feedback-into-gold flywheel.
why: Review-everything doesn't scale; review-nothing ships incidents. Risk-based sampling routes human judgment where it pays (uncertain + high-stakes + random baseline for calibration), queues respect SLAs, and reviewer UX determines throughput and log quality. Reviews are finite attention budgeted like tokens — spent where expected harm is highest.

blocks.text: Sample by risk, not by volume

Review budget covers a fraction: spend on **uncertainty** (low confidence, novel patterns), **stakes** (money, external messages, legal), plus a **random baseline** (calibration: are samplers missing whole classes?). Pure uncertainty sampling blinds to confident-wrong; pure stakes sampling wastes reviewers on routine. All three strata, proportions stated, reviewed quarterly.

blocks.caption: Three strata with stated reasons — sampling as policy, not luck

blocks.text: Queues with SLAs, UX that decides

Review queues carry **SLAs** (money items < 1h, standard < 24h) with breach escalation and aging dashboards. Reviewer UX shows: the decision, the evidence (trace + citations + diffs), one-click approve/edit/reject with reason codes — decisions in seconds, logs rich enough for gold mining. Slow UX queues rot; rich logs feed the flywheel.

Every reviewed item with its verdict returns as a **gold item** (input + expected + reviewer note): edge corrections expand edge coverage, attack attempts expand attack sets, overrides become regression tests. The flywheel compounds: reviews cost once, prevent forever. Unlogged reviews evaporate — log format designed for gold ingestion, not just audit.

blocks.title: Sample the queue
blocks.note: Run it: expect picked b,c with reasons uncertain,stakes (coverage 2/4). High-confidence routine work flows untouched; risk concentrates reviewer attention where harm concentrates.

items: Sample uncertainty + stakes + random baseline, proportions stated, reasons attached
Queues with SLAs + breach escalation; reviewer UX decides in seconds, logs for gold mining
Flywheel: reviewed items return as gold (edge/attack/override coverage compounds)

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice sampler and map picks to reasons. (b) Add the 5% random baseline stratum and argue its purpose in one sentence (what failures does randomness catch that risk-strata miss?). (c) Write the SLA pair (money vs standard) with breach actions.
hints: Baseline: b (uncertain 0.5), c (money stakes); a/d flow. Reasons travel with samples.
Random baseline catches confident-wrong and unknown-unknown classes that risk signals systematically miss — calibration against sampler blind spots.
SLAs: money <1h (breach → page + auto-hold payouts); standard <24h (breach → expand reviewer pool).
exercise.why: Stratified sampling (risk + calibration), SLA design (time + breach actions), and flywheel closure (reviews → gold) are the three review-ops judgments — attention budgeted like tokens.

quiz.q: Review queue grows unboundedly. Fix shape?
options: Risk-based sampling (uncertainty + stakes + random baseline) with SLAs + reviewer UX — finite attention budgeted by harm
quiz.explain: Unbounded queues need sampling, not staffing: risk strata concentrate finite attention where harm concentrates, SLAs bound the rest.

quiz.q: Random 5% baseline sampling seems wasteful. Purpose?
options: Calibration: catches confident-wrong and unknown-unknown classes that risk signals systematically miss
quiz.explain: Risk signals have blind spots by construction (they sample what they measure). Random slices audit the sampler itself.

quiz.q: Reviewed items vanish after decisions. Loss?
options: Flywheel fuel: verdicts with reasons become gold items (edge/attack/regression coverage) — unlogged reviews evaporate value
quiz.explain: Reviews cost once; gold items prevent forever. Log formats designed for ingestion close the loop from operations to evaluation.

summary: Sample by risk + baseline, queue with SLAs, decide via UX in seconds, log for gold. Finite attention budgeted where harm concentrates; flywheel compounds every review.
